subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He cheated in the [A] / examination, making his [B] / already-falling academic [C] / credentials worst. [D]
solution:
```html
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the word "**worst**" instead of the correct form "**worse**."
 
• The comparative form "worse" should be used here instead of the superlative form "worst".
 
• The correct phrase should be "**credentials worse**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part D** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He cheated in the examination, making his already-falling academic credentials worse."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "He cheated in the" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "examination, making his"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "already-falling academic"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part D.

``
